Retrieved 2026-07-19 via Exa. Independent published 2026-07-17 16:06 BST.

Reform could face £3m tax bill over Farage's £5m donation, tax expert claims.
- Reform UK could be hit with a £3m tax bill as a result of Nigel Farage's undeclared £5m donation from crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne (2024), tax expert Dan Neidle claims.
- Farage being investigated by Commons standards commissioner (Daniel Greenberg) for failing to declare the £5m after becoming an MP. Farage gave varying explanations (non-political; personal security; "reward for campaigning for Brexit for 27 years").
- Neidle: if a lost-earnings arrangement existed, HMRC "would have a strong argument that the 'disguised remuneration' rules apply"; Reform 2025 Ltd "would be liable for PAYE on the £5m. So about £3m." Predicated on unconfirmed Guardian report.
- Farage resigned as an MP earlier in July to trigger a Clacton by-election amid the scrutiny; standards probe paused, resumes if he is re-elected.
- Separately, Electoral Commission urged to investigate undeclared donations (2023-24) from associate George Cottrell (convicted fraudster in US); Reform rejects allegations, Farage says he acted "appropriately" and alleges an "establishment hit job".
